title: Learning-based Autonomous Oversteer Control and Collision Avoidance
abstract: arXiv:2505.15275v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Oversteer, wherein a vehicle's rear tires lose traction and induce unintentional excessive yaw, poses critical safety challenges. Failing to control oversteer often leads to severe traffic accidents. Although recent autonomous driving efforts have attempted to handle oversteer through stabilizing maneuvers, the majority rely on expert-defined trajectories or assume obstacle-free environments, limiting real-world applicability. This paper introduces a novel end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving approach that tackles oversteer control and collision avoidance simultaneously. Existing E2E techniques, including Imitation Learning (IL), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Hybrid Learning (HL), generally require near-optimal demonstrations or extensive experience. translated_title: 基于学习的自动过度转向控制与碰撞避免
translated_abstract: 过度转向是指车辆后轮胎失去抓地力并引发意外的过度横摆，这带来了严峻的安全挑战。若未能控制过度转向，往往会导致严重的交通事故。尽管近期的自动驾驶研究已尝试通过稳定化操纵来应对过度转向，但大多数方法依赖于专家定义的轨迹或假设环境为无障碍环境，限制了其在现实世界中的适用性。本文提出了一种新颖的端到端（E2E）自动驾驶方法，能够同时解决过度转向控制与碰撞避免问题。现有的端到端技术，包括模仿学习（IL）、强化学习（RL）和混合学习（HL），通常需要接近最优的示范或大量的经验积累。然而，即使是熟练的人类驾驶员也难以在过度转向条件下提供完美的示范，且高转移方差阻碍了充足数据的积累。因此，我们……
tldr: 本文提出一种新颖的端到端学习自动驾驶方法，能够同时应对车辆过度转向控制与碰撞避免，突破了现有方法依赖专家轨迹或无障碍环境假设的局限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel end-to-end learning-based autonomous driving approach that simultaneously tackles oversteer control and collision avoidance, overcoming the limitations of existing methods that rely on expert-defined trajectories or assume obstacle-free environments.
